ts.detail: escalation request caseId must be a non-empty string

findingRegister.summary: escalationRequestToMachineEvent threw a RAW TypeError on a restored snapshot: `state.ladderRound` was read before any shape check (state null -> "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'ladderRound')"), `state.challenges.filter` on a non-array ledger ("... is not a function", 344 cases) and a null ledger row ("Cannot read properties of null (reading 'bondProofHash')", 95 cases). Every other guard in the package fails closed with a typed error (assertStateArrays, r3-1/r41-1); this path did not.
findingRegister.resolution: Fixed in courtEscalationRequest.ts: the mapper now requires a record state, an array challenge ledger, and matches only rows that are objects — all typed refusals. Pinned in __tests__/differentialWire.test.ts.

findingRegister.summary: A NON-OBJECT descriptor escaped the codec as a raw TypeError: build(null) -> "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'caseId')". The r8-5 hardening ("a raw TypeError must not escape instead of this module's typed refusal") covered re-read fields but not the argument itself, and hash/build/escalationRequestToMachineEvent all reach it.
findingRegister.resolution: Fixed: buildCourtEscalationRequest refuses a non-object descriptor with the typed refusal the wire uses for a non-object body (class not_object). Pinned in __tests__/differentialWire.test.ts (build(null), build([]), hash(null)).

findingRegister.summary: "must not have leading or trailing whitespace" never said WHICH characters. The ECMAScript trim set (the shipped reading) REFUSES U+FEFF at an edge but ACCEPTS U+0085 and U+001C..U+001F, which Unicode White_Space (and Python str.isspace) treat as whitespace: a second implementer picking the Unicode set disagrees in both directions, on invisible characters, at the one place two ids must not become one.
findingRegister.resolution: Decision: the ECMAScript WhiteSpace+LineTerminator set IS the contract (the codec is the JS library and trim is its definition). Pinned in the reference (JS_WHITESPACE) and in the differential test over the union of both sets (35 characters, both edges, alone, interior). docs/DIFFERENTIAL_WIRE.md §5 D1.

repro.note: caseId prefixed/suffixed with U+0085 (accepted) or U+FEFF (refused)

findingRegister.summary: The "canonical UTF-8 (no unpaired surrogates)" refusal is not the test its message names: it is a TextEncoder/TextDecoder round-trip, and a WHATWG decoder STRIPS one leading U+FEFF, so any id beginning with a BOM is refused as "surrogates" instead of as edge whitespace. Measured on the first run: leading-BOM id -> case_id_not_canonical while the same BOM at the end -> case_id_whitespace, and a BOM-only id -> "non-empty string". Two readings of the sentence report different reasons for the same refusal.
findingRegister.resolution: Decision: the ROUND-TRIP is the contract (it is the injectivity test that matters, and both readings refuse the string), so the reference models the BOM strip explicitly. Registered as a diagnostic wart: the message names a surrogate that is not there, which sends an operator hunting the wrong character. Fixing the wording (or ignoreBOM) changes ballot-outcome validation in courtVoteMachine, a different module — out of scope, registered for the owner. Pinned in docs/DIFFERENTIAL_WIRE.md §5 D4 and in the test (leading vs trailing BOM classes).

findingRegister.summary: A JSON numeric literal is not a value. `9007199254740991.4` is read by a double parser as the integer 9007199254740991 (a safe integer, so the request is ACCEPTED and digested as that) and by an exact/decimal parser as a non-integer (REFUSED); `9007199254740993` is refused by both but for different reasons (double: 2^53 is outside the safe range; exact: ...993 is). The wire had no sentence about numeric portability, so two implementations can differ on accept/refuse for the fractional class. Modelled from the start in the reference, so the campaign never recorded it as a disagreement — a corner closed by decision, not a bug found.
findingRegister.resolution: Decision: a number field is the IEEE-754 double its literal denotes (JSON.parse semantics). Encoders must emit decimal integers in +/-(2^53-1); a fractional literal that rounds to a safe integer is accepted with the rounded value, and the canonical re-serialization carries the double. Pinned in the reference (parse_int=float) and in the test. docs/DIFFERENTIAL_WIRE.md §5 D3.
